title: Four Women Answer to This Name: Oryol to Valencia, and the Search That Came Back Empty
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Orel State University, the schooling without a year
stops.date_confidence: LinkedIn names the university and attaches no year to it; the 2012 placement is editorial, set immediately before the first attested employment, and is not an attested date
stops.campa: A LinkedIn profile under this name gives Orel State University and no year beside it. It is the same city the first attested job sits in, which is consistent and settles nothing about sequence. No faculty page carries her, no thesis, no class list, no local press. The atlas sets her here because the record begins in Oryol and because a designer employed in Oryol very probably studied in Oryol first. That last sentence is a reconstruction, and the file marks it as one rather than letting it harden into a year.
sources: LinkedIn profile under the name Daria Sorokina (designer), fetched 2026-08-12
suggested_refs: Orel State University, named without dates on the only profile that names it

stops.name: Oryol, the first line of the record
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month on the Behance resume tab; nothing earlier than this month is documented anywhere reachable
stops.campa: The record of this life opens on an employment start date. August 2012, Inventos, Oryol, Russian Federation, title Web and Mobile Designer. There is no birth date behind it, no birthplace, no patronymic, no family. A biography that begins with a job is a biography written by an employer, and this one was written by the subject herself, on a portfolio site, years later. The atlas takes what it is given: a city on the Oka, a company name, and a month.
suggested_refs: The Behance resume tab of behance.net/darsor, the only dated document in the dossier

stops.name: Inventos, Oryol, two years and five months
stops.date_confidence: the span August 2012 to January 2015 is attested; this midpoint stop is placed for travel order and carries no independent evidence of its own
stops.campa: Two years and five months at one company in a provincial Russian city of three hundred thousand. Screens, not cloth: web and mobile, layouts and interfaces. This is the whole of the evidence that puts the word Russian in her queue line, and it rests on one tab of one self-published profile. No client work from these years is named, no project survives under her name, no colleague is recorded. The corpus keeps a Russian designer in Krasnoyarsk, Ekaterina Sinchinova, nineteen years at prepress before she picked up a needle; the shape rhymes and the evidence does not touch.
suggested_refs: Inventos, Oryol, employer of record 2012 to 2015

stops.name: Oryol, the end of the salaried years
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month on the Behance resume tab; the reason for the change, and the city she was standing in when it happened, are not documented
stops.campa: January 2015 closes the only salaried position the record contains. The next line reads Freelance UI/UX Designer and gives the same month as its start, with a portfolio address instead of a company. Whether she was still in Oryol that January, nothing says. The transition is attested; the geography of the transition is not, and the atlas holds her at the last address it can defend rather than moving her early on a guess. Two dates and a change of employer are the whole documentary substance of a decade.
suggested_refs: The January 2015 line on the Behance resume, the second and last dated transition

stops.name: ETEMA.RU, the credit without a city
stops.date_confidence: undated on the source that carries it; the Oryol pin is a reconstruction, chosen because a .ru domain is the only thing locating the credit and Oryol is the only Russian address the record supplies
stops.campa: Her own site carries a co-founder and Art Director credit at ETEMA.RU. It gives no year and no city. A domain suffix is not an address, and the atlas will not turn one into a pin without saying so: this stop stands on the ground of the only Russian city the record names, and the credit itself may belong to a different year and a different street entirely. It is listed because a co-founding is the largest claim in the dossier and the least anchored.
suggested_refs: ETEMA.RU, named as a co-founding on the subject's own site, with no date and no address

stops.name: Oryol, the freelance turn
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month; everything about what the month contained is not
stops.campa: From here the record stops having employers and starts having clients, which is to say it stops being checkable. A freelance line on a resume is a claim about eleven years that no third party ever countersigned. She works, and the work is real enough to win a site-of-the-day badge seven years later, but between January 2015 and 2022 the open web preserves nothing at all: no interview, no catalogue, no institutional page, no press. The dossier is entirely self-published from this stop forward.
suggested_refs: dariasorokina.com, the address given as employer for the freelance years

stops.name: Dessau, the Bauhaus line
stops.date_confidence: wholly undated; LinkedIn states a connection to the Bauhaus Foundation Dessau and gives no year, no duration and no kind of connection. The 2015 position is an editorial guess and nothing more
stops.campa: A single line on a LinkedIn profile ties this name to the Bauhaus Foundation Dessau. It does not say study, residency, workshop, project or visit. It does not say when. It is the most interesting sentence in the dossier and the least supported, and the honest thing to do with it is leave it standing in the middle of the map with no year under it. The atlas puts her at Gropius's building for the length of one stop and takes her away again, because a foundation is not a proof.
sources: LinkedIn profile under the name Daria Sorokina (designer), fetched 2026-08-12
suggested_refs: Stiftung Bauhaus Dessau, named on the profile without a date or a role

stops.name: Valencia, the site of the day
stops.date_confidence: Behance gives the year 2022 for the CSSLight award and no month; the January date is the file's default for a year-only source, and the Valencia pin is the profile's stated location rather than the place the award was made
stops.campa: CSSLight names one of her sites Featured Site of the Day. It is the first thing in eleven freelance years that anybody outside her own pages recorded. A badge from a gallery of web design is a thin monument, and it is the monument she has: no museum accession, no press notice, no catalogue entry, no obituary in waiting. The atlas registers it at the city her profile gives, which is not the city the award came from, because awards of this kind come from no city at all.

stops.name: Valencia, the portfolio site read end to end
stops.date_confidence: the site is undated throughout; the June 2022 placement is the earliest dated item the site itself carries, and is used here as the site's own floor
stops.campa: Every page in the sitemap of dariasorokina.com was fetched and read: the front, the about, the contact, the portfolio. The site says UI/UX Designer and Art Director. It says ten years and more. It names clients by country. It names no studio and no city, which matters, because an earlier pass reported that it named both and it does not. The correction is kept in the open here rather than tidied away, since a source that was misquoted once will be misquoted again by whoever reads only the summary.

stops.name: Valencia, the CSS Winner nomination
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month on the subject's own site; the pin is her stated location, not a place the nomination happened in
stops.campa: June 2022, nominee at CSS Winner. It is the only month-precise date in the whole dossier that is not an employment transition, and it comes from the same self-published page as everything else. Two awards in one year, then silence again. The corpus knows what a designer's canon looks like when the institutions do the recording: Christian Dior has houses, dates, collections and a grave. Here the institution is a web gallery and the archive is a personal domain renewed annually.

stops.name: Valencia, the location line
stops.date_confidence: current as fetched on 12 August 2026; no arrival date, route or year of emigration is documented anywhere reachable
stops.campa: The Behance profile gives her location as Valencia, Spain. When she came, by what road, and whether she left Russia once or in stages, no source says. Ekaterina Sinchinova's file carries exactly this hole and states it in exactly these terms: no source located gives the date, the port, the reason, or the season. The same blank opens twice in one corpus, for two Russian designers who left in the same decade. The atlas does not bridge either of them, and marks the resemblance without pretending it is evidence.

stops.name: Yerevan, DASH Design Studio
stops.date_confidence: current as fetched; Behance carries the studio with no start date, and whether she has ever resided in Armenia is not stated in any reachable source
stops.campa: The company field of the same profile reads DASH Design Studio, Yerevan, Armenia. A Russian designer living in Spain with a company registered in Armenia is a sentence about the last four years of the region, and the atlas states it without extending it: registration is not residence, and no source puts her body in Yerevan on any day. The earlier pass dropped Armenia entirely and moved the studio to Spain. It is restored here to the only city the source actually names.

stops.name: Valencia, ten years and more
stops.date_confidence: self-reported and current as fetched; the claim is consistent with the 2012 start on Behance, which is the closest thing to corroboration it has
stops.campa: Ten years and more, her site says, and the Behance dates back it: August 2012 to August 2026 is fourteen. The clients are given as countries rather than companies, which is how a freelancer writes a career that has no single address. United States, Canada, Australia, the European Union, Israel, India, Russia. Seven jurisdictions, no cities, nothing mappable. The profile gives no address inside any of them, and the only city it states anywhere is Valencia.

stops.name: Valencia, the judge and the mentor
stops.date_confidence: both roles are stated in the present tense on the subject's own site with no start date; dated here to the fetch rather than given an invented year
stops.campa: She judges at Orpetron and mentors at Helper. Both roles are stated in the present tense and neither carries a year, so the file dates them to the day the page was read. A designer who sits on a jury has students and peers who know when she started, and not one of them has written it anywhere a search engine can reach. The date on these two stops therefore belongs to the fetch and not to the appointment, and a later pass that reads 2026 as a start year will be repeating a fetch log back to itself.

stops.name: Valencia, three languages
stops.date_confidence: current as fetched; self-reported and uncorroborated, like every other line on the profile
stops.campa: Russian native, English fluent, German beginner. The third one is the only trace on the profile that points at Dessau, and it is a trace and not a proof: beginner German is what a person has after a course, or after a residency, or after neither. The atlas records the three lines as they stand and refuses to read the biography backwards out of them. The three lines are self-reported like everything else on the page, and no school, course or certificate is named behind any of them.

stops.name: Ithaca, a different woman enters Cornell
stops.date_confidence: the 2004 start year is LinkedIn self-report only and could not be corroborated; the Cornell affiliation itself is corroborated independently through DBLP co-authors
stops.campa: A second Daria Sorokina is a graduate student at Cornell. She is not a designer and never was, and she is in this file for one reason: she answers to the same query and will be merged with the subject by the first pass that stops reading carefully. Her start year comes from a self-reported profile and no other source confirms it. Her existence, unlike her start year, is documented in a bibliographic database that does not take anybody's word for anything.
suggested_refs: DBLP author page pid 75/5959, the spine of this namesake's record

stops.name: Ithaca, plagiarism detection in arXiv
stops.date_confidence: attested; DBLP dates the paper to ICDM 2006 and the co-authors place it at Cornell
stops.campa: She publishes on plagiarism detection in arXiv with Johannes Gehrke and Paul Ginsparg, both Cornell, both unambiguous about where the work was done. This is the corroboration the designer's file never gets: a third party, indexed, with co-authors who can be looked up separately. One woman of this name has a bibliography. The other has a portfolio site she pays for herself. DBLP dates the paper to ICDM 2006, and that entry is where the year on this stop comes from.

stops.name: Ithaca, the additive groves
stops.date_confidence: the paper and its ECML 2007 venue are attested in DBLP; the conference city is not in the verified pool, so the stop stays at the institution rather than moving to a venue nobody sourced
stops.campa: Additive Groves of Regression Trees, by Sorokina, Caruana and Riedewald, takes the best student paper at ECML 2007. The award is the one hard, independently checkable honour attached to anybody called Daria Sorokina, and it belongs to the machine learning researcher, not to the designer. Whoever writes the next pass on this name will find it first, because it ranks well, and will be tempted. The atlas puts a fence around it here. The subject of this file has never published a paper, and this one is not hers.
suggested_refs: Additive Groves of Regression Trees, ECML 2007, best student paper

stops.name: Ithaca, the thesis
stops.date_confidence: attested; DBLP key phd/us/Sorokina08 dates the thesis to 2008
stops.campa: Modeling Additive Structure and Detecting Interactions with Groves of Trees, a doctoral thesis, 2008. A bound object with a date, a library number and a supervisor. The designer of the same name has produced nothing of this kind and, in the ordinary way of her trade, never will: interfaces are replaced, sites are redesigned, and the work of a UI designer is deleted by its own clients within a decade. The thesis is still indexed under the key phd/us/Sorokina08 and can be pulled today by anybody who types it.

stops.name: Boston, the page that confirms the award
stops.date_confidence: the faculty page is current as fetched; it lists the award without naming the year or the student, and the identification rests on the fact that the 2007 paper is his only ECML student paper
stops.campa: At Northeastern, Mirek Riedewald's faculty page lists Best Student Paper at ECML among his own honours. He has one ECML student paper and it is hers, so the award is corroborated by a source that was not written by anybody named Sorokina. It is a small thing and it is the method: find the co-author, read the co-author's page, and see whether the claim survives being told by somebody else. Applied to the designer, the same method finds nobody at all to ask.

segments.name: The Search That Could Not Find Her

stops.name: San Francisco, the four hundred and four
stops.date_confidence: the 404 is attested and reproducible; the San Francisco pin stands for the Wikimedia Foundation and is an editorial convenience, not a place any part of this life happened in
stops.campa: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daria_Sorokina returns HTTP 404. There is no article, no redirect, no disambiguation page, no stub awaiting sources. In an atlas whose other travelers arrive with encyclopaedia entries in four languages, this is the first fact about her and it is a hole. The file records the absence at the address of the encyclopaedia that does not hold her, because an absence still has to be looked up somewhere, and because a later pass should be able to repeat the lookup exactly.
suggested_refs: The missing English Wikipedia article, checked twice, 2026-08-12

stops.name: Baku, the article that answers to the name
stops.date_confidence: the article and its subject are attested; the gymnast's birth of 29 November 2002 in Baku is stated there and is a fact about her, not about the designer
stops.campa: The Russian Wikipedia does hold a Сорокина, Дарья, and she is a rhythmic gymnast born in Baku on 29 November 2002, competing for Azerbaijan. She has no connection to design, to Oryol, or to any of the four working women in this file. She is here because a search for the subject lands on her, and because an atlas that quietly let a gymnast stand in for a designer would deserve everything that followed. She was born a decade before the designer's record begins, and she holds the encyclopaedia entry outright.

stops.name: Snowshoe Mountain, what Bing returned in Cyrillic
stops.date_confidence: reproduced in the verification session; the result set is non-deterministic between runs, which is itself the finding
stops.campa: The query was Дарья Сорокина with дизайнер. Bing returned ten pages about a ski resort in West Virginia. Not a near miss, not a namesake, not a stale cache of the right person: a mountain in the Alleghenies, in English, with lift tickets. The engine is not honouring the query at all. This stop is on the map because the search physically went somewhere, and where it went was Snowshoe Mountain, four thousand miles from any city in this file. The result set does not hold still between runs either, which is the second finding and the worse one.
sources: Bing web search via WebFetch, Cyrillic query, 2026-08-12, verification run
suggested_refs: The Bing result set for the Cyrillic query, reproduced 2026-08-12

stops.name: Casablanca, the result set that would not come back
stops.date_confidence: reported by the first pass and not reproducible in the verification pass; the contradiction is left standing and neither version is adopted as fact
stops.campa: The first research pass reported that the same Cyrillic query returned pages about the film Casablanca and unrelated travel content. The verification pass ran it again and got the ski resort instead. Both cannot be the state of the index, and the file does not choose between them. What survives is the shape of the failure and not its content, which means the Casablanca detail must never be quoted again as a finding. The stop keeps the city name so that the struck claim stays findable inside this file, and labels it struck where it stands.

stops.name: Paoli, the challenge instead of an answer
stops.date_confidence: the CAPTCHA is attested for both the English and the Cyrillic query; the Pennsylvania pin is the search company's own address and is editorial
stops.campa: html.duckduckgo.com served an anti-bot challenge instead of results, in English and in Russian alike. The machine asking was a research pipeline on a home server in another country, and the machine answering decided it was not a person. Nothing about the subject was learned. This is one of the two doors that closed, and it closed on the only engine that would have answered a Cyrillic query without ranking it first for advertisers. The challenge came back for both the English and the Cyrillic query on 12 August 2026, and the endpoint was not tried a third time.

stops.name: Mountain View, the access-trouble notice
stops.date_confidence: attested for the query combining the name with художник, модельер and могила; the pin is the company's address and is editorial
stops.campa: Google was asked for Дарья Сорокина with the words for artist, couturier and grave. It returned no listing at all, only a notice about trouble accessing the service. Three of the four doors are now shut and the fourth is answering with a mountain in West Virginia. The atlas records the closures as stops because the search is the only journey this subject demonstrably made through the world this week, and it can be retraced turn by turn. The three Russian words are written out here so that somebody with a working engine can run the same query and get further.

stops.name: Oryol, two hundred of two hundred
stops.date_confidence: attested in both the research and the verification session, which reported the identical exhaustion
stops.campa: The proper search tool had nothing left. Two hundred of two hundred calls spent session-wide before this name was ever put to it, so every lookup went out through raw fetches against result pages, which return stale and cached listings and no ranking at all. The one city that would have repaid a real search, the city on the Oka where the record starts, was never properly asked about. The budget ran out before the journey reached its only ground. Both the research session and the verification session reported the identical exhaustion, so the failure is not a one-day accident.

segments.name: The Neighbours She Has Not Met

If the subject's training or career were metropolitan Russian rather than provincial, this is the pin she would inherit. It is not: her city is Oryol, three hundred and fifty kilometres south of Moscow, and no source connects her to Saint Petersburg in any year. The pin is visited so that the next pass can see it was considered and refused.

stops.name: Paris, the Russian inside the perfume
stops.date_confidence: attested for the launch of the perfume and for Ernest Beaux's Russian training; the embroidery link named in the campa is explicitly not attested in the file that carries this pin
stops.campa: Chanel No. 5 is blended by Ernest Beaux, a perfumer trained in Russia, for a house that leaned hard on Russian emigres in these years. The tempting bridge from here to any Russian woman in design is the Kitmir embroidery workshop of Grand Duchess Maria Pavlovna, and that workshop appears nowhere in the Chanel file and nowhere in this dossier. It is named here only to be refused. Coco Chanel's Paris and Oryol in 2012 are joined by nothing but a nationality.

stops.name: Paris, the couturier and the designer
stops.date_confidence: the distinction is attested in the Balenciaga file; the year is editorial, standing for the close of his house, and the verbatim wording of the quotation is not in this pool and is therefore not quoted
stops.campa: Cristobal Balenciaga drew a line between the couturier, who cuts and assembles and sews the thing with his own hands, and the designer, who only designs. Paris is where the corpus keeps that argument, together with Coco Chanel and Christian Dior. Sorokina falls on the far side of that line, in a medium the Balenciaga file never mentions: she designs objects that are not cut and not sewn, and that their owners delete on a five-year cycle. The wording of Balenciaga's own sentence is not in this pool, so it is paraphrased here and quoted nowhere.
suggested_refs: The Balenciaga distinction between couturier and designer

stops.name: Krasnoyarsk, the parallel that is only a parallel
stops.date_confidence: attested for Ekaterina Sinchinova's long prepress and graphic-design career in this city, per her own file; the parallel drawn to the subject is a structural inference and nothing more
stops.campa: Ekaterina Sinchinova trains at the Surikov college and works nineteen years in prepress and graphic design in this city before she ever touches a needle, and takes up embroidery self-taught in 2019. Russian designer who becomes something else, then leaves: it is the arc the one-line queue entry for Sorokina invites a reader to expect. Nothing in the evidence supports the expectation. The two women have a nationality, a trade and a departure in common, and no document places them in the same room.

stops.campa: Leo Chiachio and Daniel Giannone hold this coordinate for Sonoridad Amarilla, and it is the atlas's default Buenos Aires. It matters to this file only because of where her name sits in the queue: one row under Matias Carbone, the knit and crochet designer who works the dog emblem and the knot into his pieces, in a block that also holds Alberto Hugo Restrepo and a personal associate of the author. Adjacency on a list is attested. A shared city is not.
